key_provisions_or_claims: Reviews the 2015 Open Letter calling for a UN-backed international ban on offensive autonomous weapons.
Warns of an AI arms race analogous to the nuclear arms race; autonomous weapons as 'Kalashnikovs of tomorrow'.
Cites drone use in Ukraine and Nagorno-Karabakh as validation of the concerns.
Doubts a ban will succeed given opposition from major military and AI powers and enforcement difficulties.
Raises moral agency and responsibility attribution for autonomous systems, including the Uber self-driving fatality.
annotation.summary_en: Short review article supporting the 2015 Open Letter's call for a UN-mandated global ban on AI-based autonomous weapons, drawing on drone use in Ukraine and Nagorno-Karabakh. It warns of an AI arms race, doubts enforceability and political will, and discusses moral agency and responsibility for autonomous systems.
annotation.title_clean: AI, Robotics and Ethics: A Dangerous Slippery-Slope of Unmanned Autonomous Weapons Use in Modern Warfare
